question: Which surgical wound is most commonly managed by midwives after childbirth?
explanation: Midwives routinely manage surgical wounds resulting from childbirth, such as episiotomies and caesarean section scars. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is understanding normal tissue healing important for a midwife?

options.A: To prescribe strong antibiotics without a doctor
options.B: To quickly spot signs of abnormal healing and prevent infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date of the next pregnancy
options.D: To replace sterile surgical instruments during delivery

explanation: Knowing what normal healing looks like enables midwives to identify complications early and intervene appropriately. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which phase of tissue repair happens immediately after the initial bleeding stops?
explanation: After bleeding is controlled through hemostasis, the inflammatory phase begins to clean the wound bed. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h2)

question: A postnatal woman is three weeks postpartum, and her perineal tear is building new tissue and contracting. Which phase of healing is this?
explanation: Building new tissue, granulation, and wound contraction are the key characteristics of the proliferative phase. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which blood component sticks to injured vessel walls to form a temporary plug when bleeding starts?
explanation: Platelets are the primary blood components that adhere to injured vessel walls to initiate clotting. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main job of the fibrin mesh formed during the clotting stage?

options.A: To stabilize the platelet plug and seal damaged blood vessels
options.B: To destroy all bacteria entering through the skin
options.C: To prevent white blood cells from reaching the wound
options.D: To permanently replace damaged skin cells instantly

explanation: Fibrin creates a tight web that reinforces the fragile platelet plug to properly stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which white blood cells arrive first at a wound site during the inflammatory phase?
explanation: Neutrophils are the initial wave of infection-fighting white blood cells to enter an injured area. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why is mild inflammation a helpful and necessary part of tissue repair?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for collagen production
options.B: It stops all blood circulation so the tissue can rest
options.C: It permanently closes the skin gap within a few minutes
options.D: It brings infection-fighting cells and growth factors to the area

explanation: Inflammation increases blood flow to deliver white blood cells and growth factors essential for clearing debris and starting repair. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the name of the cell that produces large amounts of collagen during tissue rebuilding?
explanation: Fibroblasts are the primary structural cells responsible for producing collagen and rebuilding the extracellular matrix. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h5)

question: What gives healthy healing wound tissue its pink, grainy appearance?

options.A: The formation of tiny new blood vessels
options.B: Bacteria fighting against white blood cells
options.C: A heavy layer of dead fat cells pushing upward
options.D: Old red blood cells trapped under the skin

explanation: Angiogenesis creates a dense network of fragile new capillaries that make granulation tissue look pink and pebbled. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which type of collagen gradually replaces earlier tissue to increase scar strength during the remodeling phase?
explanation: Type I collagen provides much greater tensile strength and replaces the weaker Type III laid down earlier. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the maximum percentage of original tissue strength a fully healed scar usually regains?
explanation: Even after complete maturation and remodeling, scar tissue rarely regains full pre-injury strength, capping out around 80 percent. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which medical condition is known for slowing down wound healing in postpartum mothers?
explanation: High blood sugar and associated metabolic issues in diabetes impair immune response and collagen production. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which nutrient is especially important for providing building blocks for collagen during tissue repair?
explanation: Protein supplies the necessary amino acids required for cellular proliferation and collagen synthesis. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h8)

question: Why should midwives encourage gentle care and hygiene for postnatal wounds instead of harsh scrubbing?

options.A: To speed up the remodeling phase to finish in 48 hours
options.B: To force skin edges to remain wide open for drainage
options.C: To completely stop all natural inflammation
options.D: To prevent infection while protecting delicate new tissue

explanation: Gentle care keeps the wound clean and guards fragile new blood vessels and cells from physical damage. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h8)
